variants.title: Run the control plane
variants.context: The control plane runs five stages: immutable intake hashes the bytes, classify and route picks the path, build candidates emits typed fields with evidence, quality gates decide, and only then does a version get accepted, reviewed, or recovered. The data plane makes candidates; the control plane decides what becomes output.
variants.prompt: A tenant uploads a document bundle to the extraction service. Put the control plane stages in order.

items.text: Split the bundle into document units, identify each family, and choose the extraction path.
Check required fields, structural completeness, cross-field invariants, source coverage, and action risk.
Hash the original bytes, record tenant and source metadata, validate the file, and preserve page order.
Promote a version, send bounded work to review, quarantine the input, or replay without overwriting history.
Emit typed fields and relationships with raw spans, page regions, model identity, and calibrated confidence.

variants.hint: Which stage has to run before anything can be reproduced later?
variants.explanation: Intake fixes the identity of the bytes first, because every later stage records what it did to that exact source.

variants.title: Run the control plane
variants.context: The control plane runs five stages: immutable intake hashes the bytes, classify and route picks the path, build candidates emits typed fields with evidence, quality gates decide, and only then does a version get accepted, reviewed, or recovered. The data plane makes candidates; the control plane decides what becomes output.
variants.prompt: A supplier emails one PDF holding an invoice and a delivery note. Put the stages in order for that bundle.

items.text: The invoice is promoted to an accepted version and the delivery note is sent to bounded review.
The PDF is split into two document units and each is matched to its own family and schema.
The bytes are hashed and the page count and tenant are recorded before any renderer runs.
The invoice unit is checked for supplier identity, currency, total, and line-item reconciliation.
Each unit produces typed fields carrying page regions, spans, and the model version that emitted them.

variants.hint: A mixed PDF is not one document, and that changes where the work divides.
variants.explanation: Splitting into document units happens at classification, so each family reaches gates written for its own schema and action.

variants.title: Run the control plane
variants.context: The control plane runs five stages: immutable intake hashes the bytes, classify and route picks the path, build candidates emits typed fields with evidence, quality gates decide, and only then does a version get accepted, reviewed, or recovered. The data plane makes candidates; the control plane decides what becomes output.
variants.prompt: The stored page count does not match the manifest and the candidate is unsafe to release. Put the stages in order, ending in containment.

items.text: The route emits a candidate with typed fields and their evidence anchors.
The structure gate finds page continuity broken against the recorded intake evidence.
Intake records the source hash and the page count it actually found.
Classification selects a route for the family it believes the document belongs to.
The input is quarantined instead of promoted, and the candidate stays on record.

variants.hint: Containment is a stage outcome, not a stage the pipeline skips ahead to.
variants.explanation: A quarantine still travels the whole control plane, because the decision is made by a gate reading evidence the earlier stages recorded.

variants.title: Route before you extract
variants.context: Routing happens before the expensive path. Verify the source at the trust boundary, split and classify the bundle into document units, run the narrowest capable route, and escalate on measured evidence rather than silently emitting a partial record.
variants.prompt: A new document arrives at the ingestion queue. Put the routing steps in order.

items.text: Detect attachments and page ranges so each document family can get its own schema and owner.
Run the narrowest capable route: native text for reliable digital pages, OCR for scans, layout and table models for structure.
Escalate unknown layouts, incomplete pages, and failed gates to a stronger route, bounded review, or quarantine.
Reject or quarantine corrupt, encrypted, oversized, unsupported, or unsafe files before a parser or renderer runs.

variants.hint: Which step protects the parser rather than using it?
variants.explanation: Routing spends the cheap probe first: verify, split, run the narrowest capable route, and only then escalate.

variants.title: Route before you extract
variants.context: Routing happens before the expensive path. Verify the source at the trust boundary, split and classify the bundle into document units, run the narrowest capable route, and escalate on measured evidence rather than silently emitting a partial record.
variants.prompt: A scanned page starts on the cheap native-text route and comes back with two required fields missing. Put the steps in order.

items.text: The classifier assigns the page to a known family with a required-field schema.
The measured gap escalates the page to the stronger OCR and layout route rather than releasing a partial record.
The narrow native-text route runs first and emits a candidate with two required fields absent.
Intake confirms the file is readable and not encrypted, so it is not quarantined.

variants.hint: The fallback is triggered by measured evidence, not by a guess made up front.
variants.explanation: The narrowest capable route runs first, and escalation is justified by a gate result rather than by the file type alone.

variants.title: Route before you extract
variants.context: Routing happens before the expensive path. Verify the source at the trust boundary, split and classify the bundle into document units, run the narrowest capable route, and escalate on measured evidence rather than silently emitting a partial record.
variants.prompt: A 60 page fax arrives with a mix of application pages and unreadable cover sheets. Put the steps in order.

items.text: Page ranges are separated so the application pages and the cover sheets become distinct units.
The unreadable cover sheets are quarantined rather than merged into the application record.
The file passes MIME verification and size limits at the trust boundary.
The application pages take the OCR route sized to their image quality and language.

variants.hint: Two families in one file can end with two different outcomes.
variants.explanation: Splitting first means a bad page family can be contained without discarding the usable one.

variants.title: Compute the release metric
variants.context: Precision asks how many released predictions matched the labeled evidence. Recall asks how many labeled entities were recovered above the threshold. Review load counts the documents that entered a correction queue. One accuracy number hides all three, so each is computed against its own denominator.
variants.prompt: A labeled slice holds 300 supplier identities. The route released 240 predictions above the gate and 216 of those matched the labeled evidence. What is precision, in percent?
variants.hint: Precision is measured against what the system released, not against what the labels contain.
variants.explanation: Precision divides correct released predictions by released predictions, so 216 of 240 is 90 percent.

mistakes.feedback: That is 216 of 300, which is recall: it uses the labeled total as the denominator.
That is 240 of 300, the share of labels that got any released prediction, correct or not.

variants.title: Compute the release metric
variants.context: Precision asks how many released predictions matched the labeled evidence. Recall asks how many labeled entities were recovered above the threshold. Review load counts the documents that entered a correction queue. One accuracy number hides all three, so each is computed against its own denominator.
variants.prompt: A labeled slice holds 250 invoice totals. The route released 200 predictions above the threshold and 180 of them matched the label. What is recall, in percent?
variants.hint: Recall asks how much of the required evidence was recovered, so the denominator is the labeled set.
variants.explanation: Recall divides correctly recovered entities by labeled entities, so 180 of 250 is 72 percent.

mistakes.feedback: That is 180 of 200, which is precision: it uses the released predictions as the denominator.
That is 200 of 250, which counts released predictions rather than correct ones.

variants.title: Compute the release metric
variants.context: Precision asks how many released predictions matched the labeled evidence. Recall asks how many labeled entities were recovered above the threshold. Review load counts the documents that entered a correction queue. One accuracy number hides all three, so each is computed against its own denominator.
variants.prompt: In one day 1000 documents finish: 820 go straight through, 140 enter bounded human review, 30 are quarantined, and 10 are rejected. What percent of documents enter human review?
variants.hint: Only one of these outcomes sends fields to a person for correction.
variants.explanation: Review load counts documents whose fields a reviewer must correct or confirm, which is 140 of 1000, or 14 percent.

mistakes.feedback: That adds the 30 quarantined inputs, but quarantine means the input is broken and values must not be repaired.
That adds the 10 rejects, but a rejected input violates the contract and never reaches a reviewer.

variants.title: Name the right outcome
variants.context: Each gate outcome has a precise meaning. Straight-through promotes a version, specialist route means the general path does not cover this family, human review means bounded fields need correction, quarantine means the input evidence itself is broken, and reject means the input violates the product contract.
variants.prompt: Intake is clean and all pages are present, but a new fax-quality page family has no template in the general route and its fields land under the wrong labels. What is the correct outcome?
options: Quarantine the input until the sender agrees to change the layout.
Send the family to a specialist route built for that document shape.
Promote the candidate and let reviewers correct the mislabeled fields.
optionFeedback: Quarantine is for broken source integrity or page completeness, and neither is broken here.
Correct: the input is usable, but the general route does not cover this family reliably.
Promotion moves a wrong candidate into accepted output, and review then pays for a routing problem every time.
variants.hint: Is the input damaged, or is the route simply the wrong one for this shape?
variants.explanation: A usable input that the general path cannot model is a routing decision, so it goes to a specialist route rather than to review.

variants.title: Name the right outcome
variants.context: Each gate outcome has a precise meaning. Straight-through promotes a version, specialist route means the general path does not cover this family, human review means bounded fields need correction, quarantine means the input evidence itself is broken, and reject means the input violates the product contract.
variants.prompt: An upload turns out to be a password-protected archive that the product contract does not list as a supported input. What is the correct outcome?
options: Retry the render several times in case the encryption flag was set wrongly.
Reject the input, because it violates an explicit product contract.
Quarantine it so a reviewer can open it and extract the values by hand.
optionFeedback: Corrupt, encrypted, and unsupported files do not improve through repeated inference, so retries only burn quota.
Correct: an input outside the stated contract should not be processed further.
Quarantine holds inputs the system might still recover, and it does not authorize a reviewer to bypass the contract.
variants.hint: Is this input recoverable in principle, or outside what the product accepts at all?
variants.explanation: Reject is reserved for inputs that violate an explicit contract, which keeps quarantine meaningful for recoverable evidence.

variants.title: Name the right outcome
variants.context: Each gate outcome has a precise meaning. Straight-through promotes a version, specialist route means the general path does not cover this family, human review means bounded fields need correction, quarantine means the input evidence itself is broken, and reject means the input violates the product contract.
variants.prompt: In a claims intake flow the source is intact, every page is present, and the candidate is inspectable, but two optional dates fall below the field threshold. What is the correct outcome?
options: Infer the two dates from surrounding text and release the record.
Queue only those two fields for bounded human review.
Quarantine the document, because two of its fields failed a gate.
optionFeedback: Claims intake may accept partial data, but a system must not invent evidence a document does not carry.
Correct: an inspectable source with a few weak fields is exactly the bounded review case.
Quarantine says the input evidence is broken, which would stop a claim whose source is fully intact.
variants.hint: How much of this document actually needs a person to look at it?
variants.explanation: Review is bounded to the fields that need correction, so the rest of an intact document is not held hostage by two weak values.

variants.title: Fill in the output contract
variants.context: The output contract has four parts. Source identity says which bytes, the typed schema says which meaning, evidence anchors say where a value came from, and the decision record says why it was accepted. A model is one implementation detail inside that contract.
variants.prompt: Match each part of the output contract to what it stores.

pairs.label: Source identity
pairs.detail: Content hash, object key, ingestion time, tenant, page count, and file validation result.

pairs.label: Typed schema
pairs.detail: Versioned field names, data types, units, cardinality, required status, and normalization rules.

pairs.label: Evidence anchors
pairs.detail: Raw text, page number, span, polygon, and the nearby structure for a consequential field.

pairs.label: Decision record
pairs.detail: Parser and model versions, validator results, policy version, and the accepted output version.

variants.hint: One part answers which bytes, one which meaning, one where from, one why accepted.
variants.explanation: The four parts make a value reproducible, interpretable, inspectable, and defensible, and no model choice replaces any of them.

variants.title: Fill in the output contract
variants.context: The output contract has four parts. Source identity says which bytes, the typed schema says which meaning, evidence anchors say where a value came from, and the decision record says why it was accepted. A model is one implementation detail inside that contract.
variants.prompt: Each incident below traces to one missing part of the contract. Match the incident to the part that was omitted.

pairs.label: Source identity
pairs.detail: A retry quietly processed a newer upload and nobody can prove which bytes produced the old value.

pairs.label: Typed schema
pairs.detail: Two services disagree over whether the stored amount is in cents or in dollars.

pairs.label: Evidence anchors
pairs.detail: A reviewer cannot find the page region behind a disputed total and has to reread the document.

pairs.label: Decision record
pairs.detail: Nobody can say which policy version and validator run allowed the payment to go out.

variants.hint: Ask what question the on-call engineer could not answer.
variants.explanation: Each contract part exists to answer one question under pressure, and the incident names the question that went unanswered.

variants.title: Fill in the output contract
variants.context: The output contract has four parts. Source identity says which bytes, the typed schema says which meaning, evidence anchors say where a value came from, and the decision record says why it was accepted. A model is one implementation detail inside that contract.
variants.prompt: Match each production artifact to the contract part it carries.

pairs.label: Source identity
pairs.detail: The source_hash field that makes an asynchronous job point at exactly one set of bytes.

pairs.label: Typed schema
pairs.detail: The schema_version that keeps field migration separate from model inference.

pairs.label: Evidence anchors
pairs.detail: Cell IDs, row and column indexes, spans, and geometry kept until validation finishes.

pairs.label: Decision record
pairs.detail: The policy_version plus the compare-and-swap promotion that made a candidate accepted.

variants.hint: Two of these are version pins; decide which one pins meaning and which one pins the release decision.
variants.explanation: The job contract and the accepted-version record carry the four contract parts into operations, which is what makes replay possible.
